tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a larger disk you need to move is not the topmost on its peg, first relocate any smaller disks that are on top of it before attempting the move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk that is currently blocked by smaller disks on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 1 remains on top of it, causing an illegal source move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before issuing a move, check that the disk you intend to move is actually the topmost disk on the source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every planned move, verify the source peg's top disk matches the intended disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 from a peg where disk 1 is still on top, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the destination peg is empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the placement is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before each move, check the destination peg's top disk (if any) against the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, which is smaller, causing an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To transfer a contiguous stack of k disks from one peg to another, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a clean stack of consecutive disks between two pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a 3‑disk stack without using the recursive pattern, leading to missing or illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto a target peg, first remove any smaller disks that currently occupy that peg, so the larger disk can be placed legally.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the destination peg has smaller disks that would block a larger disk from being placed.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state and compare the resulting configuration with the goal to catch any errors before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the full sequence of moves, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg because the final state was never checked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any larger disk or an empty peg without restriction, making it useful for shuffling other disks around.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary spot to hold a disk while freeing larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failing to move the smallest disk to an auxiliary peg, causing a deadlock where larger disks cannot be moved.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as the final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Output the move list as the last list in the response and avoid any additional brackets, code fences, or text after it, so the parser reads the correct answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When formatting the final answer for submission.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending extra commentary after the move list, causing the parser to read an empty or wrong list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep move list concise to avoid token limit truncation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a short, near‑optimal sequence (e.g., by using recursion for sub‑stacks) rather than an overly long list that risks being cut off by token limits.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move sequence, aim for minimal or near‑minimal length.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing a very long move list that gets truncated, resulting in an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid blocking a target larger disk when freeing it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When you need to move a larger disk that is blocked by smaller disks, relocate those smaller disks to pegs that do not contain the larger disk you intend to move; otherwise you may end up with the larger disk still blocked and attempt an illegal move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to move a larger disk that is not currently topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 onto the same peg as disk 5, then trying to move disk 5 while disk 1 remains on top, causing an illegal source move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may finish without generating any moves, either due to early termination or misunderstanding of the output format.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always produce at least one move (or an explicit empty list if the goal is already satisfied) and ensure the move list is present as the final output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model generates a long sequence that exceeds the token budget, causing the output to be cut off before completion.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move list concise, using recursion or optimal strategies to minimize length.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk to move without checking whether it is currently the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the chosen disk is the topmost on the source peg before committing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model fails to verify that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check the destination peg's top disk (or emptiness) before each move to ensure the placement is legal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Extra list after move list causing parser to read wrong answer
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Additional brackets, code fences, or commentary after the move list confuse the answer parser, which reads the last list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Terminate the response with the move list and nothing else.
